entities.name: Anne Pépin
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Anne Pépin was the richest and most celebrated woman on the West African island of Gorée in French Senegal. Pepin’, born to a European man and African woman, was born into the Afro-European class known as habitants. In 1786, she entered a relationship with the governor Stanislas de Boufflers at the same time that he moved the capital of Senegal from Saint Louts to Gorée. Pépin held the designation of signare, a prestigious social and economic designation for women who formed partnerships with European men and, as such, wielded great power.
